title: LEUKODYSTROPHY, ADULT-ONSET, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, WITHOUT AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY

intro.text: This entry describes an adult-onset, autosomal dominant leukodystrophy in which, unlike related hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies, amyloid angiopathy is not present (Bergner et al., 2024).

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy is a leukodystrophy with adult onset.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel adult onset leukodystrophy in 16 patients from eight families
checks.explanation: Adult onset leukodystrophy is stated explicitly.

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: carrying one of four different stop-gain or frameshift dominant variants in the CST3 gene
checks.explanation: The title and abstract describe dominant variants in CST3, an autosomal gene, segregating in eight families.

checks.claim: Amyloid angiopathy is not present in adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy, unlike in related hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical and radiological features differ markedly from the previously described Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy found in patients carrying p.Leu68Asn substitution in CST3.
checks.explanation: The paper reports no angiopathy at autopsy and contrasts the disorder only with Icelandic CAA. It does not refer to related hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies in general.

paragraphs.text: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) is a neurodegenerative disorder of the cerebral white matter that begins in adulthood and is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait (Bergner et al., 2024). Brain imaging shows leukoencephalopathy. Bergner et al. (2024) found no amyloid angiopathy in the disorder, which sets it apart from hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies with white matter involvement.

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) is a neurodegenerative disorder of the cerebral white matter.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic characterization in two autopsy cases did not reveal angiopathy, but instead micro- to macrocystic degeneration of the white matter.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a leukodystrophy with degeneration of the cerebral white matter.

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) begins in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel adult onset leukodystrophy in 16 patients from eight families

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: Dominant CST3 variants cause adult onset leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper describes dominant variants in an autosomal gene.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy shows leukoencephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiologically, pathognomonic changes are found at typical predilection sites involving the deep cerebral white matter sparing a periventricular and directly subcortical rim
checks.explanation: Imaging shows white matter changes, which is leukoencephalopathy.

checks.claim: Bergner et al. (2024) found no amyloid angiopathy in adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic characterization in two autopsy cases did not reveal angiopathy
checks.explanation: The two autopsy cases showed no angiopathy, consistent with the title's 'without amyloid angiopathy'.

checks.claim: The absence of amyloid angiopathy distinguishes adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy from hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies with white matter involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical and radiological features differ markedly from the previously described Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy found in patients carrying p.Leu68Asn substitution in CST3.
checks.explanation: The abstract contrasts the disorder only with Icelandic CAA, not with hereditary CAAs with white matter involvement in general. It also bases the contrast on clinical and radiological features, not only on the absence of angiopathy.

paragraphs.text: Bergner et al. (2024) reported that adult-onset leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.

checks.explanation: The paper reports dominant variants in an autosomal gene across families.
